title: Day and Night 5
content:
Lan Wangji absorbed the over-the-top praise with deadpan serenity. Tugging open Wei Wuxian’s sleeve, he tipped the stolen stash of dates inside, announcing with utmost gravity, “For you. All of them.”

Wei Wuxian played along without missing a beat. “Well, aren't you sweet. Thanks.”

Then Lan Wangji abruptly dropped his grip. With a brisk flick of his wrist, the dates spilled out, scattering and bouncing wildly across the dirt. Wei Wuxian scrambled down to round them up, snatching up a handful only to realize dozens more were rolling away in the dark.

Lan Wangji declared flatly, “Not giving them anymore.”

Reaching down, he promptly poached the trembling hen tucked beneath Wei Wuxian’s left arm, gathering a bird in each hand like living luggage.

Wei Wuxian caught the trailing flutter of Lan Wangji’s forehead ribbon, reeling him back in. “Hey! Everything was great a second ago. What’re you pouting about now?”

Lan Wangji cut his eyes toward him, an unmistakable edge of warning hardening his gaze. “Do not pull.”

His voice was distinctly unimpressed, laced with frosty reprimand. Wei Wuxian’s fingers sprang open on pure reflex.

Chin tucked, Lan Wangji deftly juggled both bewildered hens into his left hand. Once his right was free, he patted his hair smooth and straightened the band of his forehead ribbon with fastidious care.

Wei Wuxian’s thoughts spun. Hold on. I’ve messed with his ribbon a thousand times and he’s never batted an eye. Is he genuinely pissed this time?

Deciding a little damage control was in order, Wei Wuxian pointed at the birds. “Fine, keep the dates. Just hand the chicken back, yeah? You promised me that one.”

Lan Wangji leveled a cool, assessing glare at him.

Wei Wuxian laid it on thick, dialing up his most earnest puppy-dog eyes. “Please? I really, really want it. Be a sweetheart and hand it over.”

At that, Lan Wangji’s lashes fluttered down. After a protracted pause, he reluctantly passed the original hen back.

Wei Wuxian scooped the bird under his arm, retrieved a stray date from his robes, buffed it vigorously against his chest, and took a loud, crisp bite. Since Lan Zhan wanted to run wild tonight, he might as well play along to the bitter end.

“Alright, boss,” Wei Wuxian chirped, chewing happily. “What’s next on the agenda?”

They strolled down the alley until Lan Wangji pulled up short before a clean, whitewashed courtyard wall. He checked left, checked right, and having confirmed the lane was completely deserted, drew Bichen in one fluid motion.

A flurry of dazzling azure blade-light whipped through the gloom, carving a line of bold, massive characters deep into the plaster.

Wei Wuxian leaned in to squint at the fresh gouges.

Lan Wangji was here.

“...”

Sheathing Bichen with a sharp click, Lan Wangji took a step back to admire his handiwork. Even properly plastered, his strokes retained the impeccably rigid, textbook precision of standard script. Looking thoroughly pleased with himself, he gave a curt nod of approval, paused to gather his thoughts, and raised his blade once more.

This time, he wasn't writing—he was illustrating.

A few blinding slashes flared in the dark, and a pair of stick figures enthusiastically mashing their faces together materialized on the stone.

The execution was surgical; the subject matter, downright scandalous. Wei Wuxian slapped a palm over his face with a hollow groan.

Pilfering livestock, running wild in private orchards, vandalizing public property... That settled it. Lan Wangji wasn't just acting out—he was systematically recreating every single childhood story Wei Wuxian had bragged about earlier. It was an exact match, right down to the crude graffiti!

Wei Wuxian didn't know whether to laugh or cry. Lan Zhan, you idiot... I was twelve when I did this shit!

Lan Wangji, however, was just hitting his stride. One wall wasn't enough; he was already eyeing the adjacent masonry to expand the gallery. Watching the murals morph into increasingly bizarre, unhinged territory, Wei Wuxian winced for poor Bichen’s edge. I am going to have to scrape his name off this plaster before sunrise. No way in hell can anyone link this back to Hanguang-jun. Actually, scratch that—I’ll just knock the whole damn wall down.

It took an exhausting amount of cajoling to finally herd the Second Jade of Lan back to the inn.

Wei Wuxian pawned both dazed hens off on the landlady, spinning some breezy lie about finding them wandering the streets, before dragging Lan Wangji upstairs and bolting the door.

Under the dim streetlights, the damage hadn't been fully apparent, but in the warm glow of the room's oil lamps, Lan Wangji was an absolute disaster. Downy chicken feathers, shredded foliage, and chalky plaster dust clung stubbornly to his robes, his hair, and his face. For the famously immaculate Hanguang-jun, it was an unprecedented sartorial catastrophe.

Dusting him off with affectionate amusement, Wei Wuxian laughed. “Look at you! What an absolute mess.”

Lan Wangji looked him dead in the eye. “Wash face.”

The first time Lan Wangji had gotten drunk, Wei Wuxian had washed his face for him, and the man had melted into the pampering like a spoiled kitten. Naturally, he was demanding an encore. Wei Wuxian had planned on getting him cleaned up anyway, but given the sheer magnitude of the grime, a damp cloth wasn't going to cut it.

“How about we skip straight to a bath instead?” Wei Wuxian offered, watching his face closely. “What do you think? Up for it?”

Lan Wangji’s eyes widened a fraction. He nodded instantly. “Mn.”

Of course, Wei Wuxian thought. Clean freak to his core. I’ll just lug the water up and let him handle the rest.

The inn was staffed entirely by women, and Wei Wuxian wasn't about to make the maids haul heavy buckets of scalding water up a flight of stairs. Leaving Lan Wangji seated like a well-behaved child, he slipped down to the kitchens, hauling bucket after bucket up himself. He topped off the wooden tub, swirled the water with his hand to check the temperature, and turned around to tell Lan Wangji to strip.

He froze.

Lan Wangji had already stripped down to his birthday suit, completely unprompted.

Granted, they’d bathed bare together in the freezing cold springs of the Cloud Recesses back when they were teenagers, but they’d been innocent kids back then. And the few times he’d accidentally barged in on Lan Wangji bathing since his return, his mind hadn't been straying down dangerous paths—not to mention Lan Wangji had always been submerged up to his chest.

Taking in the full, unvarnished spectacle of a naked Hanguang-jun in the flesh... the visual assault nearly short-circuited Wei Wuxian’s brain. His thoughts scrambled in a frantic loop: was he supposed to indulge his baseline urges and ogle to his heart's content, or throw a towel over the man and pretend to be a decent gentleman?

His scalp tingled with nervous heat, his boots stumbling backward on pure instinct.

Yet for every step Wei Wuxian retreated, Lan Wangji advanced.

Backed completely into a corner with nowhere left to run, Wei Wuxian was forced to stand his ground as a stone-faced, stark-naked Lan Wangji steadily closed the distance. The sharp hollow of his throat, the pale expanse of his skin, and the lean, cut lines of his physique were suddenly looming in his face. It was entirely too much. Wei Wuxian averted his eyes, swallowed hard around a dry throat, and felt a sudden, frantic wave of thirst parch his mouth.

Gritting his teeth, Wei Wuxian opened his mouth to protest, but Lan Wangji’s hands shot out—and ripped his belt clean off.

His expression remained rigidly righteous, but the execution was pure, unbridled aggression. Caught completely off-guard, Wei Wuxian leaped back, yelping, “Whoa, hold on! Stop! I’m not getting in! I’m not bathing, you go ahead!”

Lan Wangji’s brows knit into a displeased frown.

Wei Wuxian babbled defensively, “You go first! I, uh, I need more room. This tub’s a little too cozy for two, don’t you think?”

Lan Wangji cast a cool, analytical glance at the wooden tub, seemingly concurring that the dimensions were indeed lacking. Mollified for now, he sluggishly stepped over the rim, sinking beneath the surface and letting the steaming water swallow him whole.

Wei Wuxian blew out a ragged breath. “Right. Take your time and soak. I’m stepping out for some air.”

He turned toward the door, desperate for a blast of midnight wind to freeze his runaway pulse, when a heavy splash broke behind him. He spun around. “What are you getting out for?!”

Lan Wangji stood dripping on the floorboards, looking thoroughly disgruntled. “Not washing.”

“Why not? You’re filthy!”

Lan Wangji pouted in sullen silence, refusing to elaborate as he stalked toward the folding screen to reclaim his clothes. Wei Wuxian hurried back to cut him off, a sudden hunch dawning on him. “Wait... do you want me to wash you?”

Lan Wangji’s lashes dipped low. He didn't confirm it, but he didn't deny it either.

Looking at that silent, pathetic little sulk, something in Wei Wuxian’s chest melted into pure mush. Fine. I’ll just scrub his back a bit. Nothing else. Strictly business.

He took Lan Wangji by the wrist, gently nudging him back toward the water. “Alright, alright, I’ll scrub you down. Get back in.”

Docile as a lamb, Lan Wangji let himself be guided back into the tub, sliding down into the warmth. Wei Wuxian pushed up his sleeves and stepped up to the rim.

Lan Wangji’s skin was porcelain-fair, his inky hair floating like silk across the surface of the bath. Through the rising mist, he looked breathtaking—a celestial prince carved of frost and snow resting in an ethereal hot spring. Wei Wuxian almost felt it was a shame they didn't have fresh lotus petals to scatter over the water to complete the portrait.

Grabbing the wooden ladle, he scooped up warm water and poured a slow, delicate stream over Lan Wangji’s crown. Lan Wangji’s golden eyes stayed locked on his face, unblinking.

Worried the suds would sting, Wei Wuxian murmured, “Close your eyes.”

Lan Wangji ignored him entirely, keeping his gaze glued to Wei Wuxian as if petrified that blinking for a fraction of a second would cause him to vanish into thin air. When Wei Wuxian reached out to gently smooth his lids shut, Lan Wangji ducked his chin beneath the surface, blowing a sullen trail of bubbles through the water.

Wei Wuxian burst into a helpless laugh, reaching down to give his cheek an affectionate, gentle pinch. “Er-gege, how old are we today, hm?”

Plucking the soap and a damp washcloth from the tray, Wei Wuxian began working his way down Lan Wangji’s neck. As his hands traced lower, his movements ground to a dead halt.

Earlier, Lan Wangji had pulled off his own ribbon, his dark hair cascading down to mask his chest and shoulders. But now, as Wei Wuxian swept the wet, heavy strands behind his back, the exposed skin revealed over thirty savage, furrowed discipline whip scars crisscrossing his torso—and right over his heart, the dark, blistered brand of the Qishan Wen sect.

Clutching the washcloth, Wei Wuxian silently circled behind him.

The scars carved a brutal path across Lan Wangji’s back, wrapping around his ribs, his shoulders, and his arms in violent ridges over pale, flawless skin. Deep, jagged, and ugly, they permanently marred what should have been a masterwork of physical perfection.

Wei Wuxian stared in agonizing silence. Dipping the cloth into the warm water, he gently dabbed across the raised ridges of the whip marks. His touch was feather-light, terrifyingly careful, as though terrified of causing pain.

Yet these were ancient wounds. The agony had burned out years ago. And even if they were bleeding fresh, he knew Lan Wangji’s stubborn pride; the man would have bitten his tongue in half before ever letting a whimper slip or showing a scrap of weakness.

Wei Wuxian burned to ask him, right here and now, what had happened. In the entire Gusu Lan Clan, the only two men with the authority to sentence Lan Wangji to the discipline whip were Lan Xichen and Lan Qiren. What on earth could he have possibly done to drive his beloved older brother, or the uncle who had raised him with such immaculate pride, to bring down a punishment that brutal?

And that brand over his heart—a twisted echo of the iron from Xuanwu Cave that Wei Wuxian had no memory of seeing on him back then.

Yet the questions died behind his teeth. If Lan Wangji hadn't volunteered the truth while sober, Wei Wuxian refused to pry it out of him while he was vulnerable. Lan Wangji only ever dropped his guard and drank around him because of an implicit, absolute trust. Exploiting a drunken haze to dig up the man's deepest, most guarded scars would be nothing short of vile.

He had spent the entire evening plotting to get Lan Wangji drunk, sweating through an endless, exhausting round of chaos, yet he hadn't asked a single damn thing. It wasn't that he’d forgotten. The burning question had been screaming in his head the whole time: Hanguang-jun, how do you actually see me?

Yet every time the words reached the tip of his tongue, he spun some pathetic excuse to shove them back down. No rush, let him have his fun first. Don't be so casual, wait until you're sitting down properly... An endless list of stalling tactics. Stripped to the bone, the ugly truth was simple: he had chickened out.

He was terrified that the answer wouldn't be the one he so desperately wanted to hear.

Resting his forearms along the edge of the tub, Lan Wangji suddenly shifted around to face him.

Only then did Wei Wuxian snap out of his daze, realizing he’d been scrubbing the exact same patch of skin on Lan Wangji’s back for minutes on end. The flawless white flesh had been scrubbed raw and flushed, looking like it had taken a beating.

Pulling his hands back in a panic, Wei Wuxian winced. “Shit, sorry! Spaced out for a second. Did that hurt?”

His back was burning from the friction, but Lan Wangji merely offered a quiet, stoic shake of his head.

Watching him sit there so quiet, so impossibly docile, Wei Wuxian felt a fond, tender ache pinch his chest. Curling his fingers, he reached out to affectionately scratch beneath the man's chin again.

Halfway there, Lan Wangji’s hand shot out from the water, clamping hard around his wrist.
